title: Oak Creek, 2012
hookLine: six worshipers are killed at a Wisconsin gurdwara, and the sangat answers with prayer and open doors

lines: A MAN FROM THE PARKING LOT.
cards: A Sunday morning in August, in Oak Creek, a suburb near Milwaukee, Wisconsin. At the gurdwara, women are in the kitchen getting langar ready for the Sunday crowd.
A few people already sit with the Guru Granth Sahib; more families are on their way. An ordinary Sunday. Then a man walks in from the parking lot with a gun.

teach.b: On August 5, 2012, a gunman who held white supremacist views killed six people at the Sikh Temple of Wisconsin. The gurdwara's president, Satwant Singh Kaleka, tried to stop him and was killed.
So were Paramjit Kaur, Prakash Singh, Sita Singh, Ranjit Singh and Suveg Singh.
They had names. A granthi, Baba Punjab Singh, was badly wounded and died of his injuries years later. A police officer, Lieutenant Brian Murphy, was shot many times helping, and survived.
The gunman killed himself. Then the sangat held Ardas for the dead. When the police handed the building back, they cleaned the hall and opened the doors.

For weeks after, they welcomed neighbors, reporters, police officers and strangers, and fed them langar. Some had never been inside a gurdwara, and were handed a plate by the people who had just been attacked.

teach.h: A SON, AND A FORMER ENEMY.
teach.b: Since then, the community has marked the anniversary with a remembrance run named for chardi kala, rising spirits.
Satwant Singh Kaleka's son, Pardeep, later became friends with a man who had once been a white supremacist himself, and together they went into schools to talk about hate and how people leave it.
It hasn't ended: in recent years Sikhs in several countries, the US and Britain among them, have still been attacked for how they look.

If it ever happens to you or someone near you, get safe first, and call emergency help if anyone's in danger. Then tell someone, and report it; in the US, the Sikh Coalition helps. The grief was not small.
But in Sikh teaching, the sangat, the holy company, is where the Guru is found.
When it was hurt, it stayed together, and it stayed open.

how: Each August the Oak Creek sangat remembers those killed with Ardas, kirtan and a community run named for chardi kala, and the gurdwara continues to welcome neighbors to langar.

games.q: your gurdwara has just been attacked, and strangers and reporters are gathering outside. what does the Oak Creek sangat do?
o: lock the doors and keep outsiders away.
hold Ardas and open the doors, with langar.
move to a new building far away.
games.why: they held Ardas for the dead, cleaned the hall, and fed everyone who came, including people who had never been inside a gurdwara.

practice: Bring to mind the families of Oak Creek, and any community grieving now, near or far: their hall, their kitchen, their people sitting close together.

If you pray, hold them in your prayer; if you don't, simply wish them comfort and strength, and stay with them in the quiet. If this stirs up more fear or grief than you can hold, reach out: 988 in the US, or local emergency help.
